q.intro.text: Headphones cost eighty dollars. This week they are fifteen percent off.

e.intro.text: Four steps. Press each one: the picture moves first, then the notation.

e.s1.text: The original price, eighty dollars, is the whole: one hundred percent. The bar under the tag is the same eighty dollars.

e.s2.text: Ten percent of eighty dollars is eight dollars. Five percent is half of that, four dollars. So fifteen percent off is twelve dollars.

e.s3.text: Eighty dollars minus twelve dollars is sixty-eight dollars. That is the sale price, what is left to pay.

e.s4.text: Fifteen percent off leaves eighty-five percent of the bar. Eighty-five percent of eighty dollars is sixty-eight dollars: the same price, in one step.

e.why.text: Quick check: why do both ways give sixty-eight dollars?

e.w-ok.text: Yes. Fifteen percent off and eighty-five percent paid fill one hundred percent of the same price, so the two ways always agree.

e.w-luck.text: Both ways find the same part of the same bar, so they cannot disagree. Try any price.

e.w-15.text: Fifteen dollars off would leave sixty-five dollars. But fifteen percent of eighty dollars is twelve dollars.

t.intro.text: Now a forty-five dollar hoodie is thirty-five percent off. The first two steps are done for you.

t.disc.text: The discount: thirty-five percent of forty-five dollars is fifteen dollars and seventy-five cents.

t.sub.text: Your step: subtract. What is the sale price?

t.s-ok.text: Yes: forty-five dollars minus fifteen seventy-five is twenty-nine dollars and twenty-five cents.

t.s-disc.text: Fifteen seventy-five is the discount, the part that comes off. What is left?

t.s-pct.text: That takes thirty-five dollars off. The discount is thirty-five percent of the price: fifteen seventy-five.

t.s-add.text: A discount makes the price lower. Subtract the fifteen seventy-five.

t.s-zero.text: Check the subtraction across the zeros: forty-five dollars is forty-five dollars and zero cents.

t.s-other.text: Take the discount away from the original price: forty-five dollars minus fifteen seventy-five.

t.check.text: Now check it in one step. Which calculation gives the sale price?

t.c-ok.text: Yes: you pay sixty-five percent of the original. Point six five times forty-five dollars is twenty-nine twenty-five, the same price.

t.c-disc.text: Point three five times forty-five dollars is the discount, the part you do not pay.

t.c-base.text: Sixty-five percent of what? The percent is always of the original price, forty-five dollars.

t.c-twice.text: Point six five times forty-five dollars already leaves the discount out. Taking it off again counts it twice.

t.half.text: Is the sale price more or less than half of the original price?

t.h-ok.text: Right: thirty-five percent is less than half, so more than half is left. Twenty-nine twenty-five is more than twenty-two fifty.

t.h-no.text: Look at the bar: less than half comes off, so more than half is left.

t.cb-right.text: At the start you picked sixty-eight dollars, and you were right. Now you can show why.

t.cb-65.text: At the start you picked sixty-five dollars: that takes fifteen dollars off, not fifteen percent. You pay sixty-eight dollars.

t.cb-12.text: At the start you picked twelve dollars: that is the discount, not the price. You pay sixty-eight dollars.

t.cb-none.text: At the start: fifteen percent off eighty dollars is twelve dollars off, so you pay sixty-eight dollars.

p.intro.text: Riley buys a fifty dollar jacket at seventy percent off and says the sale price is thirty-five dollars. Is Riley right?

p.test.text: Let's test it. Build the argument and see where it leads.

p.prove.text: Now prove it. Fill each because with the reason that makes the line true.

p.c1.text: You pay only thirty percent of the original price, because seventy percent off leaves one hundred minus seventy, thirty percent of the bar.

p.c2.text: so the sale price is less than half of fifty dollars, less than twenty-five dollars, because thirty percent is less than half of the bar.

p.c3.text: so it is thirty percent of fifty dollars, fifteen dollars, and Riley's thirty-five dollars is the discount, because thirty-five and fifteen make the whole fifty.

p.x-bound.text: Being less than fifty dollars is not enough: every part of the bar is less than fifty dollars, the discount too.

p.x-small.text: Not here. Seventy percent comes off, so the discount is the bigger part.

p.x-disagree.text: Two correct ways to the same price cannot disagree. If they do, one has a slip.

p.x-other.text: True, but it is the reason for a different line.

p.done.text: That's a proof: three claims, each with its reason, and the picture backs every one. Riley gave the discount, not the sale price.
